subject: No-training assurance & subprocessor egress — evidence request
messages:
From: Marta Gómez <marta.gomez@medilex.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@medilex.com>; procurement@medilex.com
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: No-train assurance + subprocessor egress details

Hi Lauren,

As part of our security review for the pilot, Legal Ops asked us to obtain concrete evidence for Redwood's no-training/no-derivatives commitment plus details about how subprocessor egress is controlled. Specifically they want:  
- A short evidence pack that demonstrates requests are excluded from model improvement (logs, config flags, attestations).
- A current inventory of subprocessors that handle customer prompt/response data (roles, locations, access controls).
- Explanation of egress/export mechanisms (SFTP export vs API access), retention windows, and where export logs are stored.

Can you send a timeline for the pack and any template we should fill? We need this by end of next week to keep the procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Marta
Marta Gómez
Security & Privacy Lead
Medilex Health

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marta Gómez <marta.gomez@medilex.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com; kimberly_park@redwood.com; Legal Ops <legalops@medilex.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: No-train assurance + subprocessor egress details

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list. We can absolutely provide an evidence pack and a subprocessor mapping. High-level plan:  

1) Evidence pack (deliverable within 4 business days):
   - Operational attestation showing the no-training flag is applied at the request router level.
   - Sample audit entries demonstrating prompt/response excluded from model updates.
   - A one-page summary from our Applied ML team describing the inference-only execution path and KV cache handling.

2) Subprocessor inventory (deliverable with the pack):
   - CSV of subprocessors, their function (storage, telemetry, SFTP), country of processing, and contractual access limits.

3) Egress & export mechanics (we'll include in the ops playbook):
   - SFTP export flow vs API export: SFTP is a push-to-customer lane (files staged, retention configurable); API exports are tokenized, audited, and limited to specific service accounts.
   - Audit logs retention: default 90 days for export logs, configurable for enterprise with SLA.

I'll attach a checklist and the current subprocessor dump for Legal Ops to review. If procurement needs a signed attestation or DocuSign, say the word and we can route it to Legal.

Next steps:
- I'll assign David to generate the attestation and the sample logs.
- Kimberly will prepare the subprocessor CSV and export playbook items.

Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Trust & Safety — Redwood Inference

From: david_kim@redwood.com <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com; kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Marta Gómez <marta.gomez@medilex.com>; Legal Ops <legalops@medilex.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 08:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: No-train assurance + subprocessor egress details

Lauren / Kimberly — quick ops notes for the evidence artifacts I'm preparing:  

- Attestation: I'll produce a one-page signed attestation (PDF) that states requests marked with the customer "no_train=true" flag are not used for model improvement. This will reference the router config, the request metadata tag, and the ML ingest pipeline exclusion.
- Sample logs: I'll include 3 anonymized request IDs with timestamps showing the no_train flag and the subsequent pipeline decision (excluded). The logs will be redacted to remove PII.
- Audit trail: We'll export the audit trail for export actions (SFTP push events) covering the last 60 days. Note: audit log retention is 90 days by default; if Medilex needs a longer window we can propose an enterprise add-on.

Kimberly, can you confirm the current subprocessor CSV includes our EU-based sftp provider, the telemetry vendor, and the KMS partner? Also, for egress, add the ACLs for SFTP pushes (service account names + JIT access notes).

I plan to upload the artifacts to the shared drive and send the DocuSign link for the attestation by EOD.

-David
David Kim
Manager, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marta Gómez <marta.gomez@medilex.com>; lauren_bishop@redwood.com; david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@medilex.com>; procurement@medilex.com
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: No-train assurance + subprocessor egress details

Hi Marta — attaching the initial pack and next steps (links below).  

Included attachments (drive links & files):
- no_train_evidence_checklist.xlsx — checklist of artifacts and who produced them.
- subprocessor_inventory.csv — live export of our current inventory (roles, country, contractual clauses).
- ops-playbook-sftp-vs-api.pdf — short doc explaining export lanes and retention config.

Ask from Medilex: please confirm whether you need the attestation notarized or run through your vendor risk portal. Once confirmed, we'll send the signed DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.com/open?envelopeId=0A12B3C

Proposed timeline: artifacts uploaded and DocuSign sent by EOD today; Legal Ops review requested by Fri 12 Jun. If all good, procurement and Legal can close the SOW by next week.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Security Program Manager — Redwood Inference
